title: Hip Replacement: Does It Matter If It's Done from the Front or the Back?
metaDescription: Anterior or posterior hip replacement? What differs, what research shows about recovery and dislocation, and what to ask your surgeon.
intro: For most people the approach matters less than you may have been told. Hospital for Special Surgery says advances have all but eliminated the differences in outcomes, so the choice is mostly down to patient and surgeon preference. Your surgeon's experience and careful planning matter more.

sections.heading: What is the difference?
sections.body: Both place the same implant. The front (anterior) approach goes in through the groin and separates muscles rather than cutting them. The back (posterior) approach goes in from behind and was the main route for many years. A muscle-sparing version of the back approach also exists.

sections.heading: Is recovery faster from the front?
sections.body: Possibly a little in the first days or weeks. Hospital for Special Surgery says the front approach may mean less early pain, but the differences quickly disappear. It reports no differences in walking or return to function in a trial of about 400 patients.

sections.heading: Is one safer? What about dislocation?
sections.body: The back approach was historically linked to more dislocations, but a registry of over 2,000 matched pairs found similar rates (under 1% in both). Complication rates were low with either approach. Follow your surgeon's advice about precautions.

sections.heading: Does my body type matter?
sections.body: It can. Heavier patients tend to have the front approach, but the skin wound at the front can heal a little less well. This is something to discuss after your examination and X-rays.

sections.heading: What should I ask my surgeon?
sections.body: How often they do hip replacements, which approach they use for you and why, what precautions you will follow, and what recovery looks like for your work and home. Be cautious of anyone who promises a much faster or painless recovery.

sections.heading: When is hip replacement the right step?
sections.body: When hip pain keeps limiting your life after medicines, exercises and other treatment have been tried. It is your decision, and we explain the options without pressure.

faqs.a: It depends on your surgeon and approach; follow the instructions you are given.

faqs.q: How soon can I walk after hip replacement?
faqs.a: Usually the same or next day with support.

faqs.q: How long does a hip replacement last?
faqs.a: Modern implants often last 20 years or more.
